title: Fashion & Luxury
breadcrumb: Industries > Retail & Consumer Goods > Fashion & Luxury
meta_description: Fashion and luxury sell scarcity, story and service: assortment risk (the size-curve problem), authenticity, clienteling quality and channel consistency.

blocks.x: A no-theater description of Fashion & Luxury: what ships first, what it touches at inventory & order brokers, how it is verified, and the per SKU-store metric we commit to moving against baseline.
Before proposing anything, we map the context Fashion & Luxury will run in — regulators, decision cadence, existing contracts — because the design that ignores context fails at the gate.

blocks.title: Governed lakehouse pipeline — Fashion & Luxury
blocks.note: What the diagram shows: ingestion, transformation and serving as separate responsibilities with named owners — no stage silently trusts the one before it.

blocks.x: The architecture for Fashion & Luxury is deliberately auditable: every stage exposes its inputs, its owner and its failure policy, and the decision path shares a timeline with the audit path. Nothing important happens off the record.

blocks.x: Failure modes & the guards we ship

items: Unit costs on a published budget with alerts at the threshold — creep is caught by the meter, not by the invoice.
Contracts enforced at the boundary — schema drift fails the pipeline loudly, in minutes.
One definition per metric, owned and versioned — the dashboard and the board pack cannot disagree.

blocks.x: How we help — five priority capabilities

items: Curve modeling by door with demand transfer logic — sell-through up
Strategy through production operations — models evaluated, retrieval grounded, cost per answer owned.

blocks.x: We run Fashion & Luxury the way we run every program: the metric is signed before delivery, the pilot is bounded, and the scale decision follows the measured delta, not the momentum.
